tool.title: Tool call
tool.unknownHint: After a stop or interruption this call never reported a result: neither success nor failure is claimed.

approval.title: Permission required
approval.pendingHint: A click only submits the request; this card disappears when the backend approval.resolved arrives.
approval.resolvedSession: The backend allowed it for this session

browserApproval.title: Permission required: browser write
browserApproval.scopeHint: Allow once covers this action only; allow for this session applies per tool (not per site), and the backend still rechecks before dispatch
browserApproval.arguments: Call arguments in the authorization fingerprint
browserApproval.pendingHint: No input is dispatched until you answer; the card only disappears after you submit and the backend no longer reports it.
browserApproval.resolveFailed: Submit failed: {reason} (the card stays; retry or wait for the backend to clear it)
browserApproval.readFailed: Reading pending approvals failed: {reason} (this is not the same as having none)

browserApproval.noteApprovedSession: Allowed {tool} for this session ({origin}): the backend still rechecks every dispatch
browserApproval.noteExpired: Approval expired for {tool} ({origin}): it was not allowed and no input was dispatched
browserApproval.noteRevoked: Approval revoked for {tool} ({origin}): no input was dispatched

clarification.title: Your answer is needed
clarification.question: Question
clarification.pendingHint: This is a content question, not a tool permission: answering it grants no tool or site access.
clarification.expired: Timed out; the backend closed it as cancelled

composer.placeholder: Describe what you want done (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line)
composer.stopRequested: Stop requested: no new message is dispatched until the backend settles the run.
composer.profileHint: The backend decides which Profile this run uses
composer.modelHint: Snapshot at start; changing the model affects the next run only
composer.attachmentsHint: The backend resolves attachments: a path string is not authoritative; only backend-verified IDs and digests count.
composer.pathPlaceholder: Paste a local file or directory path

readiness.title: Cannot send yet: {count} requirement(s) unsatisfied
readiness.hint: Everything listed below is backend fact. This block re-checks automatically after you change something, and disappears once all of it is satisfied.

PI_MISSING.title: No usable Pi
PI_MISSING.detail: No Pi was found: no selected path, and none on PATH or in the common locations.
PI_MISSING.next: Install a version from the trusted manifest in Settings · Pi, or put Pi on PATH and discover again, then confirm with Select.

PI_TOO_OLD.title: Pi is below the minimum supported version
PI_TOO_OLD.next: Upgrade to {minimum} or newer in Settings · Pi; an older version cannot be used to send.

PI_UNUSABLE.title: The Pi candidate is not usable
PI_UNUSABLE.next: Pick a usable candidate and press Select, or upgrade first; an unusable candidate is never adopted silently.

PI_UNKNOWN.title: Cannot confirm whether Pi is usable
PI_UNKNOWN.detail: Discovery failed: {code}. Nothing is allowed through without a probe result.
PI_UNKNOWN.next: Press Check again; if it keeps failing, open Settings · Pi to inspect the candidates and diagnostics.

WORKSPACE_MISSING.title: No workspace registered
WORKSPACE_MISSING.detail: There is no usable workspace right now.
WORKSPACE_MISSING.next: Add a workspace in Settings · Permissions and trust it explicitly.

WORKSPACE_UNTRUSTED.title: The workspace is not trusted
WORKSPACE_UNTRUSTED.next: Trust it in Settings · Permissions: no command may run in an untrusted workspace.

MODEL_MISSING.title: No usable model
MODEL_MISSING.detail: No model is selected from the library, and the legacy provider / model fields are empty.
MODEL_MISSING.next: Define a model in Settings · Model and make it current.

MODEL_FIXTURE.title: The built-in fixture is active (scripted replay)
MODEL_FIXTURE.detail: provider {provider} / model {model}: replies are replayed from a script, not produced by a real model.
MODEL_FIXTURE.next: Pick a model from a real provider in Settings · Model; use the fixture only to self-check the pipeline.

MODEL_ENDPOINT.title: The model endpoint is a placeholder
MODEL_ENDPOINT.detail: Endpoint {baseUrl} uses port 0: a client can never connect to it.
MODEL_ENDPOINT.next: Enter a real endpoint in Settings · Model, or pick a library model that already has one.

context.empty: Nothing to show for this run yet.

agents.subtitle: An Agent is a Profile: name, model, references, permission ceiling and memory all persist on the backend.

agents.selectHint: Pick an Agent on the left, or create one.
agents.emptyHint: An Agent is a Profile: name, model, references and permission ceiling.

agents.modelHint: Only models already defined in the library can be selected.
agents.noResources: Nothing to choose from in the library.
agents.resourceUnavailable: This source could not be read:

import.urlLabel: HTTPS link to a SKILL.md or archive
import.rulesHint: Only a single SKILL.md or a zip/tar.gz over HTTPS is accepted, and the destination must be a public address (loopback, private networks, and reserved ranges are rejected). import.name: name
import.stagedHint: Content is staged in the managed directory; it is copied into the managed Skills folder only after you confirm.
import.rejectHint: Nothing is written when a link is rejected; the managed directory is untouched.
import.warningBody: Anvil never executes scripts from the archive; after you enable this Skill, the model may read them and follow their instructions.

dryrun.title: Isolated dry run
dryrun.promptPlaceholder: For example: give me an execution plan using this Skill
dryrun.warningBody: This sends a real model request to the selected provider: the prompt and the Skill content are transmitted and may cost money. The dry run uses a temporary agentDir and an empty workspace with read-only tools, no network/browser/connectors/external MCP/shell, and removes the temporary directory afterwards.
dryrun.noDenials: No tool calls were denied in this run.

limit.DRYRUN_LIMIT_USER_SKILL_DISCOVERY: Pi's user-level Skill discovery stays open: the dry run only guarantees that this one managed Skill is explicitly mounted; it does not guarantee that other user-level Skills are invisible.

memory.title: Memory
memory.subtitle: Memory is a separate section: user scope spans projects, workspace scope belongs to the current project. Disabling a scope stops injection but keeps the entries; deleting only affects future runs, and already-sent messages cannot be recalled.
memory.unavailableHint: The memory store is unavailable ({code}). This is a failure, not an empty list. Retry after fixing it.
memory.unavailableHintUnknown: The memory store is unavailable. This is a failure, not an empty list.

scopeToggle.title: Injection switches
scopeToggle.hint: Disabling only affects later retrieval and injection; no entry is deleted.

memory.tooShort: Enter at least {count} characters (fewer than {count} cannot be searched; this is not an empty result).
memory.emptyHint: Memories appear here after you save them; right now there are none.
memory.candidateHint: Candidate: joins injection only after confirmation
memory.deleteHint: Deleting only affects future injection; already-sent messages cannot be recalled.

new.title: Record a memory
new.contentPlaceholder: For example: this project uses English commit messages starting with a verb

notice.deleted: Deleted: future injection no longer includes it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Runtime settings, the Pi runtime and application updates are managed here.
settings.jumpNotice: Jumped to {section}: the requirements listed in chat are completed here.

general.title: General
general.hint: Language and theme only affect the interface; they never interrupt a running session.
general.conflictHint: The configuration was changed in another window. Reload before deciding whether to overwrite it.

model.title: Models
model.hint: Model definitions come from the resource library; secrets live only in the OS credential store.
model.emptyHint: Define a model in the resource library and set it as current.
model.deferred: Switched: a run is still active, so the new model takes effect on the next run.
model.credentialPresent: Stored in the OS credential store

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.hint: Ceilings come from system policy and the workspace; this page only shows what the backend computed.
permissions.networkUnavailable: Network access is unavailable in V1: the ceiling is always off, so there is no switch for it.
permissions.workspacesHint: No command can run in an untrusted workspace.
permissions.workspacesEmptyHint: Add a directory from chat or the workbench.

pi.title: Pi runtime
pi.hint: The host manages every Pi candidate, install and rollback on this machine; an external Pi is never overwritten or modified.
pi.emptyHint: Install a version from the trusted manifest, or put Pi on PATH and discover again.
pi.confirmHint: Candidates were detected but none is selected yet: pressing Select is the confirmation. The host never picks an external binary for you.
pi.recommendedHint: The most usable candidate according to the backend; you still have to press Select.
pi.installHint: Only versions in the trusted manifest shipped with this binary are downloaded; the UI never supplies a URL or hash.
pi.rollbackHint: Rolling back is available only when the backend confirms a verified previous version exists.

update.title: Application updates
update.hint: Updates download in the background and are installed on the next normal start; the app is never restarted for you.
update.unavailableReason: The application update service is not implemented yet (F09 is missing): there are no UpdateStatus, CheckForUpdate, DownloadUpdate, UpdateBlockers or ExitAndUpdate bindings.
update.noFakeActions: Until real state exists, this section shows no progress bar and offers no "exit and update".

security.title: Security
security.hint: Secrets are kept only by the OS credential store; this page never echoes or rewrites them.
security.storeUnavailable: Cannot confirm the OS credential store is usable: the CredentialStoreStatus binding is missing.
security.credentialsHint: Derived from the credential reference in each model definition; the secret itself is never read.
security.credentialsEmptyHint: Define a model in the resource library to see credential coverage here.
security.credentialPresent: Stored in the OS credential store
security.legacyActive: The current model comes from the legacy settings fields, so the API key is written to settings.json in plaintext.
security.legacyInactive: The current model comes from the resource library; its secret is kept in the OS credential store.
security.noSecret: Saved secrets are never displayed or rewritten here.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.hint: The diagnostics bundle is written to the local diagnostics directory and is never uploaded.

observability.title: Observability
observability.subtitle: Usage, run chains and diagnostics come from backend records; missing data is shown as unavailable, never as zero.

usage.title: Usage summary
usage.hint: Time range is RFC3339; empty means no bound. Missing usage or pricing is shown as unavailable.

run.title: Run chain
run.hint: Open by run id; anvil://observability?run=<id> also deep-links here.
run.emptyHint: Open a run from the chat run details or an anvil:// deep link.
run.listUnavailableReason: Cannot list recent runs or errors: C07 has no run-listing binding yet (only UsageSummary and RunDetails). Open a run by id.

chain.title: Event chain
chain.empty: This run has no events to show.

export.title: Diagnostics export
export.hint: Written only to the local diagnostics directory and never uploaded; content is redacted on write.

skills.title: Skills
skills.subtitle: Import from a local folder and copy it into the product-managed directory (the source folder is left untouched). Only enabled managed skills are handed to Pi explicitly via --skill; Pi's own local skill discovery stays on, so it may also load skills that already exist on this machine, and a same-name copy is not blocked by these switches (the run record keeps the two facts apart).

pending.activeRun: Skill changes saved. A run is still in progress and keeps using the old skill set; the change applies from the next run after it ends.
pending.saved: Skill changes saved; they apply from the next run.

import.hint: Importing only copies files: no script inside the skill is executed, and the dependency commands it declares are not installed.
import.pathRequired: Enter a local skill folder (or the path to SKILL.md). Importing copies the content into the product directory and leaves the source untouched.
import.donePending: Imported {name}. It applies from the next run.

state.staleInRun: A run still uses the old set

empty.title: No skills yet
empty.hint: A skill is a SKILL.md file (its frontmatter needs name and description). Only after importing it may Pi use it for a suitable task.

editor.saved: Saved. The change loads on the next run.
editor.nameHint: name cannot be changed (it is the directory name and the stable reference); re-import to rename.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.subtitle: Extensions are code that runs inside the Pi process. System policy extensions cannot be disabled; third-party extensions are off by default, and enabling one is trusting it — but trust is not a free pass on approvals.
extensions.empty: No extensions to list. This is also what you see when the system policy extension cannot be resolved — that means the repository layout is broken, not that none exist.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.subtitle: External MCP servers are connected by Pi (stdio / Streamable HTTP). The configuration only stores the command and its arguments or the url, plus credential references; disabling removes the server from the isolated agentDir's mcp.json and applies from the next run.

pending.activeRun: MCP changes saved. A run is still in progress and keeps using the old mcp.json; the change applies from the next run after it ends.
pending.saved: MCP changes saved; they apply from the next run (disabled servers are removed when the runtime is rebuilt).

mcp.diagnoseNotReady: No usable Pi is configured, so diagnosis is unavailable; the state will not be shown as connected.

badges.runningInUse: Still in use by a run

mcp.authUnsupported: MCP OAuth sign-in is not supported in V1. Save the credential as a ref and reference it through headerRefs, or authorize in an external client. This will not be shown as connected.
mcp.toolsNote: The connection is managed by Pi; the diagnosis does not include inputSchema.

credential.hint: Credentials live only in the OS keychain; the configuration stores just the ref
credential.required: Enter a credential ref and a value; the value is written to the OS keychain only and never echoed back.
credential.saved: Saved credential {ref} (the value is not echoed back and is not written into mcp.json).

empty.title: No MCP servers yet
empty.hint: stdio needs the executable and its arguments entered separately; HTTP needs a Streamable HTTP endpoint (usually /mcp). Save secrets as credentials first, then reference them in the configuration.

editor.argsLabel: Arguments (one per line; do not write shell commands)
editor.hint: Saving only validates and writes the configuration: the command is not executed and the url is not connected.

errors.idRequired: Enter a server ID (it becomes the key in mcp.json)
errors.refLine: A reference line must read NAME=ref: {line}

notice.saved: Saved {id}. Saving does not execute the command and does not connect the url.

tools.title: Tool catalog
tools.subtitle: A tool's effective state comes from configuration and Pi's diagnosis: hidden / disabled / failed diagnosis all show as unavailable. Unknown MCP tools require approval for each call; readOnlyHint is not trusted.
tools.errorTitle: Failed to read the tool catalog

empty.title: The tool catalog is empty
empty.hint: There are no tools to list right now. MCP server tools appear only after a diagnosis succeeds (Pi must connect first); the extension tool list is registered by the Pi runtime and cannot be enumerated statically.

tools.extensionUnknown: (tool list unknown; check the run record for the actual calls)

builtin.bash: Run shell commands (subject to permissions and approval)
builtin.tool_search: Activated by Pi for MCP servers with deferred exposure: search for and declare tools that are not declared yet
